I came to Tuscany for a summer job at a winery, and I never left. That was eleven years ago. Today I'm a tour guide, and I show the vineyard and the cellar to visitors from all over the world. Something funny happens on almost every tour. At the end, I ask, Any questions? and nobody says anything. Then, ten minutes later, during the wine tasting, people come to me in private and ask everything. Could you tell me how old these vines are? Do you know when the harvest starts? My favorite question is about the harvest, because I can tell the story of the grapes.

People are always surprised when I tell them our harvest is in February and March. Well, we're in Australia, so the seasons are opposite to Europe. When the grapes are ready, everything happens fast. We pick most of the grapes at night, because it's cooler, and the grapes stay fresh. Then we take them to the winery before the sun comes up. Our white wine is ready in a few months, but we age the red wine for about eighteen months, in old barrels. My grandfather started this vineyard fifty years ago. He always said that a good wine needs two things: good grapes and a lot of patience.

For years, I had the same problem on every trip. I joined tours in English, and I understood almost everything. But I never asked a question. I was always building the perfect sentence in my head, and when it was ready, the guide was already in the next room. Then a friend gave me a simple tip. Start with a short opening, like Could you tell me, or Do you know. It gives you a second to think. On my next trip, at a winery in Portugal, I tried it. I asked, Could you tell me how long this wine ages? The guide was so happy that she opened a special old wine for the whole group.
